focus: ADR-0002 node:sqlite, WAL, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, corruption policy under one shared DB, schema migration

findings.title: ADR-0002 defines no corruption policy for the shared context.db
findings.claim: v2's one-DB-per-project design (ADR-0002) states no action for SQLITE_CORRUPT / SQLITE_NOTADB. v1 had a tested policy and it does not carry over cleanly to a file now shared by many processes.
findings.evidence: ADR-0002 (docs/v2/adr/0002-single-db-git-distribution.md) lists engine, timeout, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and retention, but has no corruption-handling clause. TECH-SPEC.md:228 only lists 'integrity_check, FTS5 integrity, schema version' as a doctor check, with no stated recovery step. v1 commit 9e246a8e ('fix: WAL checkpoint on exit + corrupt DB recovery (#244)') made SessionDB rename a corrupt file to .corrupt-{timestamp} and ContentStore delete-and-recreate it ('ephemeral DB'). In v2 one file holds data for every session, agent and worktree (ADR-0002: 'Every row carries session_id, worktree and agent'), so the v1 'delete and recreate' move for ContentStore would now wipe every other agent's history too, and a rename-on-open race across 4+ live writers (GP8) is not specced.
findings.archaeology: ARCHAEOLOGY: INTRODUCED_BY 9e246a8e, 2026-04-13, 'fix: WAL checkpoint on exit + corrupt DB recovery (#244)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT (commit message): 'SessionDB renames corrupt files to .corrupt-{timestamp} for debugging; ContentStore deletes and recreates (ephemeral DB).' REGRESSION_RISK: v2 merges what v1 called the 'ephemeral, delete-OK' ContentStore and the 'durable, rename-only' SessionDB into one file (ADR-0002 §Decision 1). Reapplying v1's ContentStore rule (delete-and-recreate) to the merged file would destroy durable session history for every agent/worktree sharing the DB; reapplying only the SessionDB rule (rename) leaves no stated path back to a working DB while 4+ servers (GP8) still hold open handles on the renamed path. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: ADR-0002 must state (a) rename-only, never delete, for the shared file; (b) which process is allowed to perform the rename when multiple writers are open (compare Q6's 'last server to close' rule); (c) what the other live writers do with their now-stale file handle after a sibling renames the path from under them.
findings.fix: Add a corruption clause to ADR-0002: on SQLITE_CORRUPT/SQLITE_NOTADB, rename-only (never delete) since the file is shared; name the single process allowed to do it, matching the Q6 'last writer' rule; define what other open writers do when the path they hold is renamed out from under them; add a GP8-style multi-writer corruption test.

findings.title: No schema migration mechanism specified for the shared context.db
findings.claim: TECH-SPEC.md:228 names 'schema version' as a doctor check item, but no document states how the schema is versioned or migrated across v2 releases.
findings.evidence: grep over docs/v2/adr/0002-single-db-git-distribution.md and docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md for 'user_version', 'migration', 'migrate' returns no hits besides the bare 'schema version' doctor line. ADR-0002 §Decision 1 lists only the table names (events, sources, chunks FTS5, meta) with no versioning column or migration path, and the frequent-release model (owner decision: 'frequent releases via /release') means the schema can change often with no stated upgrade step for a file that already has rows from an older server version.
findings.archaeology: ARCHAEOLOGY: v1 never built a formal migration runner either; db-base.ts history (302bb7b8, 6b8b120e, be3cb3a9) only adds pragmas and driver fallbacks, not a user_version migration ladder. ORIGINAL_INTENT: none found — this is a gap in both v1 and v2, not a regression of a past fix. REGRESSION_RISK: low (nothing to re-break), but v2's frequent-release cadence makes the gap more likely to surface than v1's slower release pace did. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: any migration step must run inside the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE discipline ADR-0002 already requires, and must not block the 4-writer GP8 case for longer than the existing 5 s busy timeout.
findings.fix: Add to ADR-0002 or TECH-SPEC: a PRAGMA user_version check at open, with a migration step that runs once under BEGIN IMMEDIATE before any other writer proceeds, and a doctor check that reports a stale schema version distinctly from integrity_check failures.

findings.title: ADR-0002 Node minimum is still an open spike, not a checked fact
findings.claim: Decision 2's node:sqlite+timeout requirement has no confirmed minimum Node version; Q10 defers it to spike S-NODE, which TECH-SPEC §9 has not resolved in the reviewed docs.
findings.evidence: ADR-0002 Consequences: 'Which Node version is the minimum was not checked; verify-single-db.md says "Not checked: Node 22". This is spike S-NODE in TECH-SPEC §9.' DECISIONS-r3.md Q10 repeats 'set by the S-NODE spike' with no value given. This matches the prior review's open item and is not yet resolved, so it is restated here as still open rather than a new finding.
findings.archaeology: ARCHAEOLOGY: not applicable — this is a forward-looking spec gap, not a behavior inherited from v1 code.
findings.fix: Resolve spike S-NODE before release and put the concrete minimum Node version into ADR-0002 and the CI matrix; until then, mark the Node-version line in ADR-0002 as 'Open' rather than silent.
